history.new: A. Abiad, S. Butler and W. H. Haemers, arXiv:1801.01149 (2018), Section 5 'A graph product and its 2-rank behaviour', define this product (their F2 formula A1 (x) J + J (x) A2 is the symmetric-difference product; their verbal definition inverts the adjacency rule) and state that its Seidel matrix is (S1 + I) (x) (S2 + I) - I; their proof of Thm 5.1 uses its compatibility with Seidel switching. Found by the Skeptic - the lab's four searches missed it. The product itself is Harary-Wilcox (1967).
history.old: Searches (2026-10-18): 'symmetric difference' + Seidel spectrum; Kronecker product of Seidel matrices / two-graphs; tensor product of two-graphs. Only the special case with an edgeless factor, S(D_m(G)) + I = J_m (x) (S(G) + I), was found (a paper on Seidel equienergetic graphs, seen through a secondary summary). The symmetric-difference product itself is Harary-Wilcox (1967). One-line observation; plausibly known to two-graph specialists.

statement:
For all graphs G, H: S(G xor H) + I = (S(G) + I) (x) (S(H) + I), where xor is the symmetric-difference product
and S the Seidel matrix. Hence the Seidel eigenvalues of G xor H are (theta+1)(eta+1) - 1, and xor is
compatible with Seidel switching, giving a commutative associative product on two-graphs with unit [K1].
title: The symmetric-difference product is the Kronecker product of Seidel matrices; it acts on two-graphs
